questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A singer writing corridos about women who fought back against attackers
A Grammy-nominated producer reviving mariachi bands for tourists
A Oaxaca conference campaigning for Mexico's first woman president
An Indigenous girls' brass band touring churches for a Netflix show
questions.explain: Vivir Quintana writes corridos about women who fought back, driven by her friend's murder.

questions.q: What did Quintana want to be before a music teacher heard her sing at 11?
questions.explain: She dreamed of becoming a chemist.

questions.q: How did the newspaper describe the death of Quintana's friend Sandra Rivera?
questions.explain: The headline read 'Students Die After Love Pact', though there was no love pact.

questions.q: How long did it take Quintana to write 'Canción Sin Miedo' after Mon Laferte asked her?
questions.explain: She locked herself in her studio and came out nine hours later.

questions.q: Why does Quintana likely write corridos about women who killed their attackers?
options: She was once imprisoned for defending herself against an attacker
She wants to challenge the stigma women face for fighting back
She hopes to win over the drug traffickers who dominate corridos
She plans to run for Congress on a platform of prison reform
questions.explain: She said women who kill are stigmatized as 'murderous women' and she wanted to use music to do something about it.
